source.title: Real-time detection and localization of honeycomb defects in concrete pillars using hybrid deep learning models
source.authors: Sourav Das; Biswarup Yogi; Raj Majumdar; Pritha Ghosh; Satyabrata Roy

record.file_problem: Full article text is present. It contains a malformed training-algorithm sentence, but Table 2 states batch size 16 and 50 epochs.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for a trained hybrid detector on a concrete-defect image dataset, a new setting for the broad training-error claim. It does not test the specified random-initialization recipe or CIFAR benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports one training accuracy result relevant to training classification performance. Other detection and segmentation metrics, and comparisons among models, do not measure the claim's training-error outcome. The algorithm text says “0 epochs,” while Table 2 says 50 epochs; no resolution is given.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a pretrained defect-detection and segmentation pipeline, without testing any specified optimization claim. Its 98.26% training accuracy does not test V1's random-initialization setting. It cites Gilmer et al. when introducing loss curves but measures neither curvature nor learning-rate stability thresholds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that the hybrid pipeline provides accurate honeycomb detection and localization and outperforms individual models, while acknowledging imperfect calibration and misclassifications.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pre-trained YOLOv5 and Mask R-CNN on a concrete-defect dataset, with a hybrid detection and segmentation pipeline; the claim version concerns sufficiently large convolutional networks trained from random initialization on CIFAR benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: The pretrained hybrid pipeline reportedly achieves 98.26% training accuracy and 97.80% validation accuracy on PHDD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pretrained YOLOv5 and Mask R-CNN pipeline can achieve high reported training accuracy on concrete honeycomb classification.

fits_no_version.finding: The loss-curve discussion describes declining training and validation losses over 20 epochs, without numerical endpoints, learning rates or curvature measurements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed pipeline exhibits reported loss convergence during training.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the training accuracy. The reported training recipe is inconsistent: the algorithm prose says 0 epochs, while Table 2 says 50. Model size and initialization details are not stated beyond describing pre-trained models.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure training classification error. Detection and segmentation metrics, validation accuracy, and comparisons with other models were left out because they do not separately report the claim's training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Training sufficiently large networks from random initialization with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/100; random or corrupted labels; effects of size, stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima and effects of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, matched identity-shortcut comparisons and the specified initialization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature changes and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Matched comparisons with and without batch normalization, learning-rate tolerance and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: Missing optimization experiments are untested components, not evidence limiting a version. Pixel-value normalization is not a batch-normalization experiment. Training duration is inconsistently described as 0 epochs in malformed prose, 50 for YOLOv5 in Table 2, and 20 in the loss-curve discussion.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses a concrete-defect dataset rather than CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100; does not report training from random initialization, corrupted or random labels, model size, SGD or Adam, or effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization. It reports training accuracy rather than training classification error.

rows.subject: Proposed Hybrid Model (YOLOv5 and Mask R-CNN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained the hybrid model on the Pillar Honeycomb Defect Dataset; the article describes pre-trained models and gives conflicting epoch counts.

conditions.value: Pillar Honeycomb Defect Dataset (PHDD); 1600 training images
reported for the model trained on PHDD

rows.locator: Dataset description; Experimental result analysis, page 8; Table 2, page 9
rows.note: Training accuracy implies nonzero training error, but the value is high. The study does not identify a random-initialization recipe. The algorithm description says “0 epochs,” while Table 2 gives 50.
rows.check: The reported 98.26% training accuracy is correctly extracted, but it concerns pretrained YOLOv5 and Mask R-CNN on PHDD. It cannot establish V1's effect under training from random initialization. Nonzero error alone also does not justify 'partial' for a claim allowing near-zero error. The supporting confusion-matrix counts total 2992 cases, inconsistent with the stated 1600 training images.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
